raw.assessment: The incumbent works relatively well under stable assignments: seven-minute median handling versus 17 overall, with only 32/40 exports containing intended courses (D1-O1/O2). Current-assignment lookup could explain six affected exports, but causation is unproven (D1-O3). The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. Replacement waits greatly exceed execution time without identifying the bottleneck (D1-O5). No observed cross-center rows establishes only the sampled result; split-course behavior remains untested (D1-O4).

openings.claim: Current instructor assignments may distort historical-week course selection; resolving assignments for the requested week could reduce omissions.
openings.delta: Tests temporal selection as the cause of the assignment-change association.
openings.prediction: Holding attendance, names and requested week fixed, changing only current assignment changes exported course membership; week-specific lookup preserves the agreed historical set.
openings.probe: Replay fabricated staging cases before and after reassignment, comparing selected course IDs under both lookups. Include cross-center decoys, verify documented CSV compatibility, and exercise simultaneous attendance entry. Time-box investigation within the six engineer-days before selecting implementation.
assumptions: Authoritative assignment history is available within the engineering and hosting limits.
Intended weekly membership can be established independently of the export.

openings.claim: Do renamed courses disappear from export selection, or do coordinators fail to recognize courses already present?
openings.delta: Distinguishes selection failure from reconciliation failure in the supplied rename counterexample.
openings.prediction: Selection failure leaves underlying course IDs absent; recognition failure leaves them present but flagged. A stale timetable instead disagrees with independently agreed intended membership.
openings.probe: Use consenting coordinators' short sessions with fabricated unchanged and renamed cases. Establish intended courses, inspect internal IDs privately, observe spreadsheet actions, and time checking versus importing. Preserve the documented CSV. Use findings to choose a bounded remedy and evaluate the next-40-export targets.
assumptions: Internal course identity is inspectable without CSV changes.
Sessions and analysis fit the first-change budget.

raw.assessment: Historical assignment projection and name-based reconciliation may generate replacement demand. Associations justify tests, not causal conclusions. These bounded probes do not establish production feasibility or the success targets.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for a requested week may destabilize historical course selection. Feedback edge: reassignment changes the exported course set, generating discrepancy checking and replacement requests.
openings.delta: Test week-specific course selection as a way to remove demand created by the assignment rule.
openings.prediction: With attendance and intended week fixed, changing only instructor assignment changes incumbent course inclusion. Holding selection to the intended week's roster prevents that difference. Unchanged inclusion weakens this mechanism.
openings.probe: In private staging with fabricated participants, establish intended course sets with coordinators. Export before and after reassignment; compare with explicitly week-scoped selection. Keep attendance entry available and verify center isolation and the documented CSV schema. Estimate historical-data availability and deployment effort before extending the experiment.
assumptions: Assignment affects selection; this is unproven.
A correct week-specific roster can be established for staged cases.
Both probes together fit six engineer-days and existing hosting; deployment remains conditional on feasibility.

openings.claim: Does comparing course names with independently maintained timetables generate replacement requests for renamed courses whose attendance is already present? Feedback edge: reconciliation creates apparent omissions, prompting another file that reproduces the ambiguity.
openings.delta: Distinguish missing-data demand from demand for recognizable course identity.
openings.prediction: For identical complete attendance rows, a verified old-name/current-name link reduces false omission reports and replacement requests. Actual missing rows remain detectable. Equal error rates weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Use consenting coordinators' two short sessions for counterbalanced fabricated examples, with and without a private companion name mapping. Include complete renamed courses and genuinely missing courses. Observe checking time, omission decisions and replacement requests separately. Preserve the CSV schema; keep all material inside authorized workspaces.
assumptions: Renames can be linked accurately within a center.
Mappings do not resolve course splits or stale timetables.
Session improvements require confirmation across the next 40 exports.

openings.claim: Current-assignment lookup may omit historical courses, generating checking and replacement demand.
openings.discriminator: Changing only assignment changes incumbent membership; week-specific lookup preserves intended membership. Unchanged inclusion weakens causality.
openings.fit: Private staging; compatible CSV, isolation and concurrent-entry checks.
openings.probe: Agree intended sets independently; replay fabricated reassignments under both lookups with cross-center decoys; estimate history availability and deployment effort.
openings.uncertainty: Association is unproven; authoritative history, intended membership and deployment feasibility remain uncertain.

openings.claim: Renames may cause selection loss or apparent omissions that regenerate replacement demand; stale timetables offer another explanation.
openings.discriminator: Absent internal IDs indicate selection loss; present IDs flagged absent indicate recognition failure; timetable disagreement needs independent membership. Mapping should reduce false reports while preserving missing-course detection.
openings.fit: Private authorized workspaces; unchanged CSV; uninterrupted attendance.
openings.probe: Counterbalance fabricated unchanged, renamed and missing courses, with/without companion name mapping, across two short sessions. Inspect IDs; observe spreadsheet actions, checking/import time, omission decisions and replacement requests.
openings.uncertainty: Identity inspection and accurate mappings are assumed. Mappings cannot settle splits or stale timetables; unchanged errors weaken recognition causality.

lineage.reason: With A1; temporal test and feasibility retained.
With Z2; mapping and missing-course control retained.

post_distill.decision: Bound both probes to six engineer-days and existing hosting; deployment conditional. Split-course isolation and replacement-delay bottlenecks remain unresolved. Synthetic evidence proves no remedy: confirm next-40 targets of median handling <=12 minutes, >=95% intended sets, zero cross-center records.
